cues.say: Component 17: Hosted checkout + webhooks. Customers pay on the payment provider's page. The provider then calls your server (a webhook) to say the payment worked. You'll bring this up during version one, wherever you call an outside service.
Think of it as: Letting the bank's own teller handle the cash. Use it for every payment.
Here's a real scenario. Order 42 (24 dollars) at the pizza shop.
Without it: Your own card form puts card numbers on your servers.
With it: Create a Stripe Checkout session; the customer pays there.
Check signature, save event id, mark paid, reply OK fast.
Same event again later? Known id: ignore it.
Why it works: You never touch card numbers, and the webhook tells you about a payment on someone else's page.
In the interview, say: Card data never touches our servers, which shrinks our PCI scope.
A few related terms you may hear.
Webhook: The provider calling your URL when something happens.
Webhook rules: Check the signature (proof it's Stripe), reply OK fast, do the work later, ignore repeats, expect some late.
PCI: Security rules for handling card data.
Test mode: Fake payments, for load tests.
Rate limit: About 100 requests a second by default. Ask for more before launch.
SMS, email: Same pattern: call from a worker, respect the limits.
